learnings: Models with aggressive safety filters may flag standard Linux system administration files (like sysusers.d, tmpfiles.d) containing words like 'user', 'group', or 'root' as unsafe. The audit tool should filter out safety-category rejections that don't map to actual code execution or injection risks.
Transcription artifacts like HTML entities (e.g., '&&') in PKGBUILDs should be recognized as formatting/hygiene issues and ignored by the security assessment logic.
Tool errors (empty LLM responses) should be isolated so they don't unnecessarily escalate the entire package audit to 'inconclusive' when other models have successfully reviewed the files.
